nodes.text: Does there exist $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}\subset \mathbb{N}$ which is a minimal basis of order $2$ (i.e. every large integer is the sum of $2$ elements from $A$, and no proper subset of $A$ has this property), such that\[\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{a_k}{k^2}=c\]for some $c\neq 0$?

#326 : [ErGr80,p.47] number theory | additive basis Erdős originally asked this for any basis (not necessarily minimal); such a basis was constructed by Cassels [Ca57] . Erdős and Graham conjectured a negative answer to this question.
